plants.name: Camellia japonica
plants.description: An evergreen shrub with glossy dark green leaves and rose-like flowers that brighten the winter garden. Hundreds of cultivars exist, with single, semi-double, and fully double forms.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to early spring (peak in midwinter in warm temperate zones)
plants.location: Native to Japan, Korea, and China; widely cultivated in the southeastern United States, Europe's mild coastal regions, and Australia
plants.funFact: Camellia japonica is closely related to Camellia sinensis, the plant used to make tea, and its seeds are pressed to produce camellia oil used in cooking and hair care.

plants.name: Helleborus niger
plants.description: A low-growing perennial with nodding, cup-shaped white flowers that emerge in the coldest months, often pushing through snow. Its leathery, dark green leaves persist through winter.
plants.location: Native to the mountains of central and southern Europe; grown in temperate gardens of Europe and North America
plants.funFact: Despite its name, it is not a rose but a member of the buttercup family, and all parts of the plant are toxic.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: A dramatic shrub producing the largest flower head in the Protea genus, with a bowl of showy pink bracts surrounding a center of fuzzy flowers. It thrives in fynbos habitat with nutrient-poor soils.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to summer in the Southern Hemisphere, with flowering often from November to February
plants.location: Native to the Western and Eastern Cape of South Africa; cultivated in Australia, Hawaii, and California
plants.funFact: It is the national flower of South Africa, and its thick underground lignotuber allows it to resprout after wildfires.

plants.name: Hippeastrum vittatum
plants.description: A bulbous perennial that sends up tall stalks bearing several large trumpet-shaped flowers. Often forced indoors in the Northern Hemisphere for winter bloom, and blooming outdoors in summer in the Southern Hemisphere.
plants.bloomingSeason: Winter indoors in the Northern Hemisphere; summer outdoors in the Southern Hemisphere
plants.location: Native to the Andes and South America; cultivated worldwide as a houseplant and garden bulb
plants.funFact: The bulbs can bloom again year after year, and a single bulb can produce multiple flower stalks that reach over 60 cm tall.
